title: Erdős #1147: Additive Basis from Diophantine Approximation

problemStatement.formal: \text{Is } A = \{n \geq 1 : \|\alpha n^2\| < 1/\log(n)\} \text{ an additive basis of order 2?}
problemStatement.plain: Let α > 0 be irrational. Is the set A = {n ≥ 1 : ‖αn²‖ < 1/log(n)} (where ‖·‖ denotes distance to nearest integer) an additive basis of order 2? Answer: NO (Konieczny [Ko16b]).
whyMatters: Connects Diophantine approximation with additive combinatorics
Shows that sets defined by approximation quality can be too sparse for additive structure
Measure-theoretic result: fails for almost every α

proven: Konieczny [Ko16b] disproved for almost every α
Generalized: any ε(n) → 0 gives the same failure
Set is infinite for any irrational α (by Dirichlet's theorem)
open: Are there specific α where the set IS a basis?
